schema:name: DCP's chapter-scoped definition of a major immigrant neighborhood, and SoHo-Little Italy's figures under it
schema:text: The New York City Department of City Planning, in The Newest New Yorkers, 2026, Chapter 3, states: "Neighborhoods that have both a large number of immigrants, as well as high immigrant concentrations, are defined as major immigrant neighborhoods. To qualify as a major immigrant neighborhood in this chapter, foreign-born density had to exceed the city average—a threshold of 40 percent was used—and the 20 neighborhoods with the largest foreign-born populations were then selected." The same chapter's Manhattan neighborhood table records SoHo-Little Italy with a total population of 22,167, a foreign-born population of 6,769, and a foreign-born share of total population of 30.5 percent -- below the 40 percent threshold.
dcterms:description: High confidence because the definition is quoted from the Department of City Planning's own retrieved report chapter and the figures are re-derivable from its embedded table. A small margin remains for the table-parsing step.
